question: A developer needs a field's value to be automatically calculated from other fields on the same record, and wants that calculated value to already be present in the database — and visible to a Client Script's onLoad handler — by the time the form finishes loading. Which approach fits, and why?

choices.text: An 'after' Business Rule, since it runs closest to when the user will view the record
A 'before' Business Rule, since it runs before the write completes and can set the field's value so it's already persisted when the record is next read
An 'async' Business Rule, since asynchronous execution is fastest
An onLoad Client Script alone, since it runs before the user sees the form

explanation: A 'before' Business Rule runs before the database write completes, letting it modify the current record's fields so the calculated value is part of what actually gets persisted — an onLoad Client Script only runs client-side after the record is already loaded, and an 'after'/'async' rule runs too late (or unpredictably relative to the read) to guarantee the value is already saved.
pieges: Assuming a Client Script can substitute for server-side, persisted calculation — it only affects what's shown in the browser, not what's stored.
Choosing 'async' by assuming it means 'faster and therefore better', when async execution isn't guaranteed to complete before the record is next read.
